caption: Technician privileges at a glance. On HF you get CW-only slices of 80 m (3.525–3.600 MHz), 40 m (7.025–7.125 MHz), and 15 m (21.025–21.200 MHz), plus 10 m (28.0–28.5 MHz): CW and data on 28.0–28.3 MHz — where the automatic propagation beacons live at 28.2–28.3 MHz — and SSB phone plus CW on 28.300–28.500 MHz, all at 200 W PEP maximum. On VHF and up you share the same allocations and modes as every license class: 6 m (50–54 MHz), 2 m (144–148 MHz), 1.25 m (219–220 and 222–225 MHz), 70 cm (420–450 MHz), and more bands above, with a 1500 W PEP general ceiling (some specific restrictions apply). The bottom 100 kHz of 6 m and 2 m is CW only.
